entities.summary:
Sakir-Har was a Hyksos king of the early Fifteenth Dynasty of Egypt, ruling over parts of Lower Egypt during the Second Intermediate Period, possibly in the early 16th century BC.

As a ruler of the Hyksos dynasty, Sakir-Har played a key role in the political landscape of ancient Egypt during the Second Intermediate Period, a time of great upheaval and instability.

Sakir-Har's reign is notable for its association with the rise of the Hyksos dynasty, a group of Semitic invaders who established themselves in Egypt around 1650 BC and went on to play a significant role in shaping the country's history.

Sakir-Har's legacy extends beyond his own reign, as he contributed to the development of the Hyksos dynasty's military and administrative structures, which would go on to influence the course of Egyptian history for centuries to come.

In the annals of Egyptian history, Sakir-Har's name serves as a reminder of the complex and often fraught relationships between different cultures and empires, and the lasting impact that these interactions can have on the development of human civilization.
